scope: C1 source observation only; approved scope remains 200 each A1-C1
source_limitations: Oxford dictionary entry definitions/POS/register observed directly, but dictionary page presence is NOT a CEFR label. Only affable and conscientious show topic Personal qualities c2/c1 respectively; topic CEFR is NOT interchangeable with core Oxford 3000/5000 list membership. Cambridge pages were inaccessible directly (HTTP 403), indexed publisher excerpts are secondary leads. No independent Myanmar, English, example or level reviewer signed off.

records.shortlist_english_definition: Friendly and easy to speak to.
records.shortlist_myanmar_meaning: ဖော်ရွေပြီး စကားပြောဆက်ဆံရလွယ်ကူသော
records.shortlist_example: Despite his senior position, the director remained affable with new staff.
records.source_observation: Oxford entry describes a person who is approachable and pleasant; topic Personal qualities carries c2.
records.editorial_risk: formal-register? no explicit formal tag on Oxford entry; C2 topic label is not proof of Oxford 5000 membership.

records.shortlist_english_definition: Careful to do work thoroughly and responsibly.
records.shortlist_myanmar_meaning: အလုပ်ကို တာဝန်သိစွာ အသေးစိတ် ဂရုတစိုက် ဆောင်ရွက်သော
records.shortlist_example: A conscientious inspector records even small defects in the report.
records.source_observation: Oxford entry describes doing tasks carefully and correctly; topic Personal qualities carries c1.
records.editorial_risk: C1 topic tag is consistent with draft level but does not independently validate translation or example.

records.shortlist_english_definition: Cheerful willingness and speed in doing something.
records.shortlist_myanmar_meaning: အလုပ်တစ်ခုကို စိတ်အားထက်သန်ပျော်ရွှင်စွာနှင့် လျင်မြန်စွာ ဆောင်ရွက်လိုစိတ်
records.shortlist_example: The volunteers responded with alacrity when help was requested.
records.source_observation: Oxford formal uncountable noun entry emphasises enthusiasm or happiness; Cambridge indexed entry additionally highlights speed and eagerness.
records.editorial_risk: Draft Burmese conveys cheerful speed and willingness; reviewer should check whether 'speed' and 'happiness' are both essential in the exact teaching sense.

records.shortlist_english_definition: Difficult to understand because the ideas are unusually complex.
records.shortlist_myanmar_meaning: အယူအဆများ အလွန်ရှုပ်ထွေး၍ နားလည်ရခက်သော
records.shortlist_example: The lecturer explained the abstruse theory with a simple diagram.
records.source_observation: Oxford describes difficult-to-understand content and marks it formal, often disapproving.
records.editorial_risk: Draft definition adds unusual complexity as the cause; reviewer should check whether that restricts the meaning and whether C1 is supported.

records.shortlist_english_definition: To speak unclearly in order to avoid giving a direct answer.
records.shortlist_myanmar_meaning: တိုက်ရိုက်အဖြေမပေးလိုသဖြင့် မရှင်းမလင်း လှည့်ပတ်ပြောဆိုသည်
records.shortlist_example: The witness began to equivocate when asked about the missing documents.
records.source_observation: Oxford formal verb entry describes intentionally unclear speech to avoid or hide truth; Cambridge indexed entry confirms intentional ambiguity.
records.editorial_risk: Draft example with witness may imply dishonesty; reviewer must check example grammar, transitivity and natural Myanmar translation.

records.shortlist_english_definition: To make information deliberately difficult to understand.
records.shortlist_myanmar_meaning: သတင်းအချက်အလက်ကို ရည်ရွယ်ချက်ရှိရှိ နားလည်ရခက်အောင် ရှုပ်ထွေးစေသည်
records.shortlist_example: Technical jargon can obfuscate the real reasons for a delay.
records.source_observation: Oxford formal verb entry describes making something harder to understand, usually deliberately; Cambridge indexed entry includes intentional and non-intentional use.
records.editorial_risk: Draft definition says deliberately but example 'Technical jargon can obfuscate...' does not establish intention. Align exact sense, definition and example before approval.

records.shortlist_english_definition: Calmness and self-control during difficult situations.
records.shortlist_myanmar_meaning: ခက်ခဲသော အခြေအနေများတွင် တည်ငြိမ်စိတ်နှင့် မိမိကိုယ်ကို ထိန်းချုပ်နိုင်မှု
records.shortlist_example: She handled the unexpected criticism with remarkable equanimity.
records.source_observation: Oxford formal uncountable noun describes calmness without anger or upset, especially in difficulty; Cambridge indexed entry agrees.
records.editorial_risk: Draft Myanmar adds self-control; reviewer should distinguish inner calm from deliberate emotional suppression. No word-specific CEFR label visible.

records.shortlist_english_definition: A feeling of emotional relief after expressing strong feelings.
records.shortlist_myanmar_meaning: ပြင်းထန်သော ခံစားချက်များကို ဖော်ထုတ်ပြီးနောက် စိတ်ပေါ့ပါးသက်သာလာခြင်း
records.shortlist_example: Writing about the experience gave him a sense of catharsis.
records.source_observation: Oxford specialist noun entry describes emotional release and relief, often through art.
records.editorial_risk: Draft writing-example may be valid broader usage; reviewer must check specialist register, exact sense and pedagogical suitability for C1.
